title: Lake Biofilms Sampling for DNA Analysis and Microscopic Counts
author: Frederic Rimet
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.br2xm8fn

steps.title: Select Sampling Season and Sites
steps.instruction: Choose the sampling period and locations based on environmental conditions and lake geography.

substeps.instruction: Perform sampling during summer.
Select sites free of submerged and emergent macrophytes to avoid shadowing effects.
Ensure water levels have been stabilized for at least 3 weeks.
If strong waves or storms scoured biofilms, wait 2-3 weeks before collecting samples.
Sample at 50 cm depth from the minimum annual water level.
Select at least 10 stations per lake, typically every 0.5 to 1.5 km along the shoreline.

In homogeneous shorelines, maintain the 0.5 to 1.5 km spacing; in heterogeneous areas, increase site density near river mouths, wastewater treatment plants, harbors (inside and outside), or quarry exploitations.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Prevent Contamination
steps.instruction: Apply cleaning precautions to avoid DNA contamination.

substeps.instruction: Use new nylon brushes (e.g., toothbrushes).
Clean the lab tray with 10% H2O2, rinse with DNA-free water, and dry.
Wear gloves throughout the process and change them between different sampling stations.

steps.title: Collect Biofilms from Stones
steps.instruction: Collect biofilm samples from stones if available.

substeps.instruction: Collect at least 5 stones (depending on size/biofilm amount) for a total brushed surface of at least 100 cm².
Take stones at 20-50 cm depth from the minimal annual water level within a 100 m² area (e.g., a 2 m wide strip over a 50 m stretch).
Let stones drain for a few minutes.
Fill the bottom of the tray with 50 ml of DNA-free water.
Brush the top and sides of the stones in the tray, avoiding the surface that was in contact with the ground.

steps.title: Process Stone Biofilm Samples
steps.instruction: Sub-sample the biofilm/water mixture for DNA and microscopy analysis.

substeps.instruction: For DNA samples: Transfer 10 ml of the mixture into a tube, add ~40 ml of absolute ethanol to reach a total volume of 50 ml, shake to homogenize, and label.
For microscopy samples: Transfer 10 ml of the mixture into a second tube and add either 70% Ethanol or 2% Formaldehyde as the preservative.
For live microscopy (soft algae): Keep a third 10 ml sub-sample without fixation.

steps.title: Collect Biofilms from Alternative Substrates
steps.instruction: Use alternative methods if stones are unavailable.

substeps.instruction: For artificial/hard substrates (e.g., riprap, concrete banks): Use a hoe equipped with a net to scrap a minimal surface of 100 cm³ at 20-40 cm depth.

For macrophytes: At 20-40 cm depth, squeeze submerged filaments (e.g., Elodea, Potamogeton) or scrap at least 20 cm of macrophyte stem (e.g., Typha). Note: Indicate 'macrophyte' on the sample label; these are for diatom analysis only.

steps.title: Prepare Blank Samples
steps.instruction: Create a blank sample for DNA analysis to monitor contamination.

substeps.instruction: Create approximately 1 blank sample for every 10 stations.
Fill a clean tray with 50 ml of DNA-free water.
Transfer 10 ml of this water into a sterile 50 ml Falcon tube.
Complete the tube with ~40 ml of absolute ethanol to reach 50 ml.
Shake to homogenize and label.

steps.title: Store and Document Samples
steps.instruction: Label, store, and document all collected materials.

substeps.instruction: Label samples with: 'Biofilm', 'River Name', 'Station', and 'Date'.
Store DNA and blank samples at 4°C in the dark for max 1 month, or frozen at -20°C or -80°C for max 3 months.
Store microscopy samples at ~ +4°C in the dark.
Complete field sheets including Station description (A), Sample description (B), Shore description (C), and Land use description (D).
Provide photographic documentation of the sampling area if possible.
